verdict.rationale: Aider's own documented behavior keeps the user's work in open, portable formats. Every AI edit is committed to the user's local git repo with a descriptive message. Options live in a plain `.aider.conf.yml` file or `AIDER_xxx` environment variables. Nothing locks the user in, but there is no documented export feature. Missing for 10: any documented export of chat/session history or other Aider-held data, an explicit data-portability or exit statement, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message.
/git will let you run raw git commands to do more complex management of your git history.
Most options can also be set in an .aider.conf.yml file... Or by setting environment variables like AIDER_xxx
